Subject: Proposal: Per-region commit sizing + replication options

Hi Amelia / Leo,

Thanks again for taking time yesterday — attached is the proposal we discussed. The per-region pricing table (attached) shows two packaging options:

- Active-Active (hot): separate dedicated GPU pools in both regions, traffic routed by policy, full replication of model weights and KV caches.
- Active-Passive (async DR): primary region handles traffic, second region kept as warm standby with async replication of weights and periodic KV seeding.

A few clarifying notes up front:
- Per-region minimums are expressed as committed GPU units (vGPU-equivalent). If you commit to two regions hot-active, you commit the minimum in both regions.
- For async/passive DR we can offer a reduced per-region minimum (typically 40% of hot-active) because the standby doesn't need full baseline throughput.
- Cross-region routing has two cost components: inter-region egress (cloud bandwidth) and capacity for routing failover. We show both in the table.

Attachments: Acme_Redwood_Proposal_Q2_2027.pdf, per-region-pricing-table.xlsx, mutual_action_plan.md

Can you review the per-region numbers and call out which failover topology (hot-hot vs hot-standby) you prefer? I can put together a concrete quote with staged commit terms if you want to see a discounted tier for a multi-region commit.

If helpful, we can do a short 30-min ops walkthrough with our infra engineer to go over traffic shaping and SLOs.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Stephanie — proposal looks comprehensive. A couple of clarifying questions before we loop procurement:

1) Per-region minimums: your table lists 80 committed GPUs per region for hot-active and 32 for async-standby. Is the standby minimum guaranteed to 32 regardless of load, or can that fluctuate as a % of primary? We are looking for cost predictability.

2) Discounting: we are evaluating committing to two regions (US-West + US-East) over a 12-month window. What kind of commitment discount can you offer if we commit to a 2-region active-passive pattern vs 2-region active-active?

3) Cross-region routing/egress: can you quantify monthly egress costs you expect for a distribution of 70/30 traffic with occasional failover (assume failover tests monthly)? We need a ballpark for Procurement.

4) Throughput guarantees: what SLOs do you provide for cross-region routing/reroute times and cold-start when the standby is promoted?

We'd appreciate an example line-item quote showing: (A) hot-hot 2-region commit, (B) hot-standby 2-region commit with DR credits, and (C) a staged ramp option where committed capacity grows over 9 months.

If you can get that by EOD tomorrow we can start procurement review early next week.

Best,
Amelia Ross

Folks, forwarding Acme's questions — they want:
- clarification that standby minimum (32) is fixed in contract or can be a %
- a discount schedule for a 2-region commit (hot-hot vs hot-standby)
- egress estimate for 70/30 traffic split and monthly failover tests
- SLOs for promotion/cold-start

My read: they want strong cost predictability. Procurement will push for lower guaranteed minimums in each region; we can counter with staged commits + DR credits.

Suggested options to price:
A) Hot-Hot 2-region: standard commit (80 GPUs region), NO standby credit. Discount 15% on base unit price for 12-month upfront.
B) Hot-Standby: primary commit 80 GPUs, standby commit 32 GPUs with 30% DR credit applied to standby for first 6 months. Discount 20% on overall committed spend if they sign a two-region commitment (12 months).
C) Staged ramp: 6-month ramp where first 3 months standby billed at 20% of standby rate, months 4–6 at 60%, then full. Offer termination protection (90-day notice) and an SLA credit pool for miss.

Questions for pricing/finance:
- Can we extend a higher % discount on standby-only capacity if procurement insists on lower primary commit?
- What's our estimate for inter-region egress per TB between US-West/US-East (use committed network spec) so we can ballpark the monthly egress figure?

Attaching Acme's email below for context.

—Stephanie

Amelia — thanks for the clear list. We ran numbers with finance and infra and assembled three concrete options (summary below). Full line-item PDF attached and I included a short mutual action plan (MAP) with timelines.

Summary (US-West + US-East) — all are 12-month legal terms unless noted:

Option 1 — Hot-Hot (active-active)
- Per-region committed: 80 GPUs each
- Unit price: standard list
- Discount: 15% off base for 12-month upfront
- No standby credits
- Estimated inter-region egress (70/30 traffic distribution): ~12 TB/month -> estimate $1,050/month (cloud egress + routing overhead)
- SLO: 99.5% availability per region; failover routing target < 30s for policy-based routing (in-path checks)

Option 2 — Hot-Standby (recommended for cost predictability)
- Primary committed: 80 GPUs (US-West)
- Standby committed: 32 GPUs (US-East), billed at 70% of full standby price for months 1–6 (DR credit), then 100% thereafter
- Discount: 20% on committed spend when committing to both regions under the staged schedule
- Estimated inter-region egress with monthly failover tests: ~3–5 TB/month -> estimate $420/month
- Promotion/cold-start expectation: median promotion time (with warmed checkpoint) ~45–90s; worst-case cold bootstrap ~4–6 minutes (documented rollback plan)

Option 3 — Staged Ramp (9-month ramp)
- Month 1–3: standby billed at 20% of rate; Month 4–6: 60%; Month 7–9: 80%; Month 10+: full.
- Discount: 18% average effective over year if they accept staged ramp and 9-month commit schedule
- SLA credit pool for missed latency/availability targets (details in attached MAP)

Additional commercial concessions we can offer if Acme signs by May 12:
- Waive the first 3 months of cross-region egress charges up to 10 TB total (on us)
- One complimentary ops walkthrough (30–45 min) with infra lead and a load test run
- DocuSign link for electronic signature; standard procurement-friendly terms in the attached PDF

Next steps:
1) Which option do you want pricing formalized on (we'll return a final redline-ready quote)?
2) If Option 2 or 3, confirm which region you want as primary for month 1 and whether monthly failover tests are acceptable.
3) We'll open the procurement SOW and route the DocuSign.
